newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday July 23.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi says in an interview that he is preparing a new development programme for this autumn including incentives to sectors like building, research and services. Prodi also repeated he was confident Italy would join the first wave of Economic and Monetary Union (La Stampa).
* A military court handed former Nazi SS captain Erich Priebke a five-year sentence for his role in Italy's worst World War Two atrocity, but freed his co-defendant, former major Karl Hass (all).

* Italian shares surged to new record highs on Tuesday, with the all-share Mibtel index closing 2.06 percent higher and hitting a record high of 14,928. The Italian September BTP LIFFE futures contract also hit a fresh all-time high of 137.65, with the spread between cash 10-year BTPs and German bunds narrowing to a record 87 basis points (all).
* Preliminary data from another six sample cities after the five of Monday showed consumer price inflation rose 1.6 percent year-on-year in July compared with 1.4 percent in June (all).

* The Treasury said a group led by Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) bought a stake in telephone directory publisher Seat for 1.58 trillion lire. Stock market watchdog Consob had previously said ordinary and savings shares in Seat, up for sale after being spun off from telecommunications giant STET, were suspended on the Milan stock market for Tuesday's trade pending an announcement (all).

* State-controlled energy group ENI is poised to acquire a significant minority stake in Albacom, a telecom venture currently owned jointly by British Telecom, Italian banking group BNL and media group Mediaset. Sources close to the negotiations said ENI is expected to acquire a stake of around 35 percent in Albacom SpA. British Telecom declined to comment on the report (Il Sole 24 Ore)
* Industry minister Luigi Bersani confirmed that energy group Ansaldo, part of state-controlled Finmeccanica, was studying the possibility of co-operation with South Korea Daewoo (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
